assets.content:
Subject: The signup that loads no new page
Preview text: Why a page-based goal can miss the conversions you most want to count

Hi there,

Most signup tracking keys on a page load — the thank-you screen, the confirmation URL that appears when someone finishes.

If your signup completes inside the app without ever loading a distinct page, that approach never records it. You end up undercounting exactly the signups you're trying to judge.

Plausible is a privacy-friendly analytics dashboard with two goal types. A pageview goal matches a URL. A custom event goal captures the signup as an event sent the moment it fires — through a small snippet or the Events API.

Yes, that event needs a line of code. Once it's in place, the goal reports alongside your traffic sources and entry pages, so you can see which ones bring in real signups.

The official goal-conversions guide walks through how both goal types are set up and what the Goals section reports. Read it and you can pick the one that fits how your own signup flow finishes.

Read the goal-conversions guide →

- the Plausible Analytics team

emails.job: Get the reader to open the official goal-conversions guide and understand that one signup goal will show them how many real trial signups they get and from which sources and landing pages.
emails.single_idea: Set up one signup conversion goal and your dashboard will show how many real trial signups you get and which sources and landing pages drive them.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.why_it_fails: A raw signup total can be inflated by bot and spam traffic and attributes nothing, so it can't tell the owner which source or landing page is working or how real the spike was.
emails.mechanism: Once Plausible's script is on your site, you mark the page a visitor lands on after signing up as a pageview goal — no extra code. From then on the Goals section reports that goal's conversions broken down by referrer source and entry page, and bot, referrer-spam and data-centre traffic is filtered out of the box so the count reflects real human visits.
